//source: This manuscript arrived as a legacy binary .doc and was converted with `soffice --headless --convert-to docx` (docs/GETTING-STARTED.md). That conversion stamps <w:numPr><w:numId w:val="0"/></w:numPr> — OOXML for 'numbering explicitly removed' — onto ordinary paragraphs, which the importer used to read as 'this is a list item'. That is fixed in the engine (hasListNumbering() in import-docx.js), not here, because it will recur for every .doc-sourced manuscript.
//manuscript-correction: APPLIED DIRECTLY TO THE .docx, and it must be re-applied if that file is ever re-converted from the original .doc. The manuscript's copyright line was typed '@Zambia Educational Publishing House' — an '@' for '©', and missing the year. Corrected to '© Zambia Educational Publishing House (2026)', the exact form the Learner's Book and every other 2026-cycle manuscript here uses. This cannot be done with an override: the engine finds the imprint page by looking for '©' or 'All rights reserved', so with the '@' spelling the copyright line fell BEFORE the detected imprint start and was swept into the cover block's byline array as a second 'author', where the cover's name filter discarded it. It never reached the block list that overrides operate on. Recorded here because books-to-typeset/ is git-ignored, so the edit itself is invisible to version control. The author should carry this into the next issue of the manuscript.
//authors: Same byline defect as the Learner's Book: the manuscript's cover byline is one 44-character string ('Francis Siakumena and Mirriam Mhone-Muzona'), which the cover's author filter drops as too long, leaving only the single name recovered from the AUTHORS bio section — so the cover and title page read 'AUTHOR: Francis Siakumena' and dropped the second author entirely. Split into two so both are credited. The second name is spelled WITHOUT the hyphen the manuscript uses — Mirriam Mhone Muzona — on the author's own instruction, matching the Learner's Book.
